newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - New deals meeting strong demand.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - New deals meeting strong demand.

text.p: Five companies went public in the U.S. markets Wednesday and all met strong enough demand to send the prices of their newly minted shares rising.
Waterlink jumped 20 percent after the water purification company's initial public offering, making it the top percentage gainer on the New York Stock Exchange.

The stock rose 2-7/16 to 13-7/16 from its IPO price of $11, the middle of a pricing range of $10 to $12. The Canton, Ohio, company sold 4.5 million shares, raising $49.5 million. Smith Barney was the lead underwriter.
Also going public was a bank, a maker of three-dimensional media processors, a real estate company, and a Chilean holding company that owns a copper company and a brewer.
Demand was solid for most of the deals in the first few hours of trading.
-- Quinenco SA, the 21st company from Chile to trade on Wall Street, rose 11/16 to 18-11/16 in heavy trading, with 2.3 million shares changing hands by midday.
Quinenco is the holding company for Luksic Industrial Group, which owns stakes in copper products maker Madeco and brewer Compania Cervercerias Unidas.

-- Life Financial Corp, a chartered stock savings bank, rose 2-3/8 to 13-3/8 in its debut on the Nasdaq. The shares were priced conservatively at $11, the middle of a range of $10 to $12. IPO analysts had forecast the stock would pick up $0.50 to $0.75 at its opening.
